intro: FOMC Decision Day — Warsh's first press conference at 2:30 PM ET is the week's binary. VIX at 18.28 has breached the <17 conditional-add gate; rate hike odds for 2026 have repriced to 50–68% on prediction markets. These are FOMC-conditional ideas: the lean shifts sharply based on the dot plot. For session June 18, the setup is: bull scenario (neutral dot) = most ideas flip to buy; bear scenario (hawkish dot) = reduce risk, extend the XLE short, BTC stop nears. SK Hynix's new ATH is the one unconditional bull item this morning.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: Post-FOMC add at $210–$220 if Warsh delivers a neutral dot — highest-conviction reactivation trade in the portfolio.
ideas.why: The conditional add framework (VIX <17, Iran deal, 30Y <5%) is one gate away from full reactivation: VIX needs to close below 17 post-Warsh. The fundamental case is unimpeached — $25B bond sale, SK Hynix locked through 2030, $91B Q2 consensus. A neutral dot compresses VIX in the same session. The setup is buy the confirmation at $210–$220 with the $195 stop already defined.
ideas.trigger: Warsh press conference neutral dot (≥1 cut in 2026 median) → VIX compresses below 17 → add at $210–$220 on the same session.
ideas.risk: Hawkish dot (zero cuts + hike markers) extends the VIX spike above 20 and tests $200–$205. Do not add into the presser.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: New ATH breakout — hold the core, add on any post-FOMC KOSPI pullback to ₩2,350,000–₩2,380,000.
ideas.why: SK Hynix broke its June 2 ATH of ₩2,407,000 cleanly to ₩2,425,000 on above-average volume this morning, confirming the price-discovery move the brief has been anticipating. The HBM shortage running through 2028 (TradingKey) and the shareholder value enhancement disclosure are new catalysts. The ~38-analyst consensus PT of ₩2.52M is only 3.9% above the new ATH, with PT upgrades likely. This is the one unconditional bull item in the morning regardless of FOMC.
ideas.trigger: New ATH already confirmed. Any post-FOMC KOSPI pullback to ₩2,350,000–₩2,380,000 is the add window. Stop: ₩2,280,000.
ideas.risk: Hawkish Warsh spikes the dollar, weakens KRW, and a profit-taking wave from the ~54% foreign float hits the stock at the ATH.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: FOMC binary — BTC below $65K is the yellow flag; either the trigger reclaims on a neutral dot, or the stop ($63,500) comes into play on a hawkish one.
ideas.why: BTC slipped below its own $65,000 re-risk trigger to $64,657 ahead of the FOMC. Rate hike odds at 50–68% and a P/C ratio of 0.98 signal the options market is already positioned for the downside. The next 3 hours either validate the regime (neutral dot → BTC reclaims $65K, HOLD upgrades to BUY) or confirm the break (hawkish dot → flush toward $62K–$63K stop zone). There is no edge in adding pre-Warsh.
ideas.trigger: Neutral FOMC dot → BTC reclaims $65K and holds → upgrade to buy. Hawkish dot → reduce before $63,500 two-day stop.
ideas.risk: The crowded long book with P/C 0.98 and funding recently negative means a hawkish outcome is a flush, not a slide.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Wait for the FOMC volatility to deliver the hedged entry at $195–$200 that Day 3 briefly flashed.
ideas.why: SPCX's June 16 intraday low of $195.13 touched the identified pullback entry zone, then reversed viciously to close $201.80. Day 4 at $208 is above every entry zone. Options IV is compressing from 85% to ~65–70% on Day 2 — in 1–2 sessions (Thursday/Monday), spreads normalize enough for a put hedge to be mechanically viable. FOMC today could be the catalyst for the next $195–$200 dip. Wait for it with the hedge ready.
ideas.trigger: SPCX pullback to $195–$200 + front-week put spreads normalize to <1.5pt ATM → enter with protective put defined-risk structure.
ideas.risk: The MSCI passive bid overwhelms the FOMC sell pressure and SPCX rips to $225+ again — the entry zone never materializes and the discipline holds.

ideas.name: SPDR Energy Select Sector ETF
ideas.idea: Short the Iran oil repricing — energy earnings estimate cuts are coming regardless of FOMC outcome.
ideas.why: WTI ~$80 and Brent ~$80 are structurally below the $87–90 embedded in energy equity valuations at the start of June. H2 2026 energy sector earnings estimate cuts of 8–12% are mathematically inevitable at current oil prices and have not yet materialized on the Street. A hawkish FOMC is an incremental tailwind for this short: risk-off sessions hit commodities and energy equities together. The Hormuz reopening is a structural shift, not a temporary spike — the energy repricing is multi-week, not intraday.
ideas.trigger: Continue scaling short at $53–$56; any Brent bounce to $83–$85 on mine-clearance headlines is the better short entry, not the exit.
ideas.risk: Iran deal collapses entirely AND Brent closes above $90 on two consecutive sessions — cover immediately.

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: Best-positioned megacap for a post-FOMC rally if the dot is neutral — self-funded AI, clean balance sheet, momentum.
ideas.why: Among the megacaps, Meta has the cleanest combination: AI capex funded internally, no debt issuance required, strong momentum, and fundamentals the market is rewarding rather than questioning. In a post-neutral-FOMC relief rally, META is the likely megacap leader. At ~$576, it has consolidated after recent highs — the setup is to buy the confirmation if Warsh delivers.
ideas.trigger: Neutral Warsh dot → broad-market risk-on → META holds $570 support and breaks higher on momentum.
ideas.risk: 30Y above 5.00% post-Warsh brings the multiple headwind back immediately for long-duration growth assets including META.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: Psychologically disrupted by SPCX briefly overtaking its market cap — FOMC determines whether that's noise or signal.
ideas.why: SPCX briefly exceeded Microsoft's market cap intraday on June 16 (fully diluted ~$2.8T vs MSFT ~$2.7T). This is not a fundamental event but it is a sentiment one — momentum sellers may target MSFT as an 'overpriced incumbent' narrative if SPCX's AI pivot story gains traction. FOMC determines whether MSFT's multiple expands (neutral dot) or contracts (hawkish dot). Azure AI thesis is unchanged; the entry is post-FOMC dip to $385–$392.
ideas.trigger: Post-FOMC neutral dot + VIX compression + MSFT pullback to $385–$392 → buy.
ideas.risk: Hawkish dot re-rates long-duration multiples; MSFT is not immune despite the quality of its franchise.
